name: Silver Fox
description: Silver Fox is a China-nexus threat cluster best known for mass-distributing Winos 4.0 (also tracked as ValleyRAT), a modular Gh0stRAT-derived remote access trojan, primarily via trojanized installers, malicious search-engine ads, and DLL sideloading targeting Chinese-speaking users. Throughout 2025 the group escalated with a Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) campaign abusing a Microsoft-signed but unblocklisted WatchDog Anti-Malware driver (amsdk.sys) to kill EDR processes before deploying ValleyRAT, and expanded geographically into Japan, Malaysia, and Taiwan via HoldingHands RAT and tax-season spear phishing. In May-June 2026, Securelist and The Hacker News reported a new tax-themed phishing wave against Indian and Russian organizations (industrial, consulting, retail, transportation) using fake Income Tax Department notices and modified Rust loaders to deliver ValleyRAT alongside a previously undocumented Python-based backdoor, ABCDoor â€” which supports persistence, screenshotting, remote keyboard/mouse control, file operations, and clipboard exfiltration. The group's blend of high-volume opportunistic phishing with kernel-level evasion tradecraft and rapid international expansion makes it one of the most actively reported China-linked clusters right now.

ttps.notes: Tax-themed lures impersonating Income Tax Department notices, delivered as archive attachments containing 'list of tax violations'

ttps.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
ttps.notes: Modified Rust-based loaders sourced from public repositories used to download and execute ValleyRAT
Trojanized legitimate applications/installers used to side-load malicious DLLs that launch Winos 4.0/ValleyRAT
BYOVD abuse of Microsoft-signed WatchDog Anti-Malware driver (amsdk.sys) to gain kernel-level access

ttps.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
ttps.notes: Vulnerable signed driver used to terminate EDR/AV processes prior to payload execution
ABCDoor backdoor communicates with C2 over HTTPS to receive tasking and exfiltrate data
ABCDoor harvests and exfiltrates clipboard contents from infected hosts
ValleyRAT plugin acts as loader for Python-based ABCDoor backdoor

notable_techniques: Tax-season phishing lures impersonating national tax authorities (India's Income Tax Department, Russian equivalents) with fake 'tax violation' archives
BYOVD abuse of a Microsoft-signed WatchDog Anti-Malware driver (amsdk.sys) not present on Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist or LOLDrivers at time of campaign
One-byte modification of vulnerable driver binaries to generate new file hashes while preserving valid Microsoft signatures, evading hash-based blocklists
Trojanized popular Chinese-language software installers and DLL sideloading as primary initial-access vector for Winos 4.0
ValleyRAT used as a multi-stage loader/plugin platform â€” most recently to deliver the previously undocumented Python-based ABCDoor backdoor
Rapid geographic expansion in 2025-2026 from Chinese-speaking targets into Taiwan, Japan, Malaysia, India, and Russia via HoldingHands RAT and ABCDoor
High-volume email blasts (1,600+ malicious emails in a single campaign window) against industrial, consulting, retail, and transportation sectors
detection_opportunities: Inbound emails referencing tax audits, tax violations, or income tax notices with archive attachments containing executables or Rust-compiled loaders
Loading of unsigned or rarely-seen kernel drivers, especially amsdk.sys (WatchDog Anti-Malware) or other Zemana SDK-based drivers, outside normal software deployment
Sudden termination of EDR/AV processes immediately preceding unexplained outbound connections â€” indicative of BYOVD-based defense impairment
DLL sideloading patterns: legitimate signed executables loading DLLs from non-standard or user-writable directories
Outbound HTTPS beaconing with periodic clipboard-sized data transfers, consistent with ABCDoor exfiltration behavior
Process trees showing Rust-compiled loader binaries spawning network connections followed by secondary payload execution (ValleyRAT/Winos 4.0)
Endpoint telemetry showing Gh0stRAT-family C2 protocol characteristics (custom packet headers, XOR-obfuscated traffic) from Winos 4.0/ValleyRAT implants
response_playbook: Flag inbound 'tax violation' or audit-themed emails with archive attachments containing executables.
Hunt for loading of unsigned or rarely-seen kernel drivers (especially amsdk.sys / Zemana SDK-based) outside normal deployment.
Alert on sudden EDR/AV process termination immediately preceding unexplained outbound connections (BYOVD impairment).
Check signed executables for DLL sideloading from non-standard directories.
Inspect outbound HTTPS traffic for periodic clipboard-sized transfers (ABCDoor exfiltration pattern).
Look for Gh0stRAT-family C2 protocol characteristics (custom packet headers, XOR-obfuscated traffic) from Winos 4.0/ValleyRAT.
